summary: 奥克兰的 Talbot Park 在旧公屋社区衰败后进行改造。增加住宅密度的同时，设计者借可视边界、多样户型和更密切的租务管理，回应安全与不同家庭的需要。

paragraphs.brief: 公共住房也能兼顾品质
sentences: The new Talbot Park is immediately eye-catching because the buildings look quite different to other state-housing projects in Auckland.
改造后的塔尔博特公园一眼就能吸引人，因为其建筑面貌与奥克兰的其他公共住房项目十分不同。
‘There is no reason why state housing should look cheap in my view,’ says architect Neil Cotton, one of the design team.
设计团队的建筑师尼尔·科顿说：「在我看来，公共住房完全没有理由看起来很廉价。
‘In fact, I was anticipating a backlash by those who objected to the quality of what is provided with government money.’
我原本还担心，有人会不满用公帑提供这么高品质的住宅，因而强烈反弹。」
The tidy brick and wood apartments and townhouses would not look out of place in some of the city’s most affluent suburbs, and this is a central theme of the Talbot Park philosophy.
这些整洁的砖木公寓和联排住宅即使放在城里最富裕的郊区也不会突兀，这正是塔尔博特公园设计理念的核心。
paragraphs.gist: 塔尔博特公园的砖木住宅并不显得廉价，放在富裕城区也很协调，正体现了设计团队对公共住房品质的坚持。

paragraphs.brief: 早期花园与紧密的邻里关系
sentences: Talbot Park is a triangle of government-owned land, which in the early 1960s was developed for state housing built around a linear garden that ran through the middle.
Talbot Park是政府拥有的土地的三角形，1960年代初期，该地被开发成一个围绕一个直线花园建造的国家住房，该花园穿过中间地带。
Initially, there was a strong sense of neighbourliness.
最初，人们有一种强烈的睦邻精神。
Former residents recall how the garden played a big part in their childhoods — a place where kids came together to play softball, cricket and bullrush.
老住户回忆起，花园在他们童年里占了很重要的位置，小伙伴在那里打垒球、板球，也玩集体追逐游戏。
‘We had respect for our neighbours and addressed them by title — Mr and Mrs so-and-so,’ recalls Georgie Thompson, who grew up there in the 1960s.
六十年代在这里长大的乔治·汤普森回忆：「我们尊敬邻居，总是以姓氏加先生或太太来称呼他们。」
paragraphs.gist: 上世纪六十年代初建时，住宅围绕一条长花园布置，孩子们在那里玩球，邻里互相尊称，老住户回忆起的是紧密的社区联系。

paragraphs.brief: 居民隔阂、失修与改造决定
sentences: Exactly what went wrong with Talbot Park is unclear.
塔尔博特公园到底出了什么问题还不清楚
The community began to change in the late 1970s as more immigrants moved in.
随着更多的移民进入，社区在1970年代后期开始变化。
The new arrivals didn’t always integrate with the community and a ‘them and us’ mentality developed.
新来者有时未能融入原有社区，逐渐形成了区分「他们」和「我们」的心态。
In the process, standards dropped and the neighbourhood began to look shabbier.
在这一过程中，标准下降，该居民区开始显得更加破旧。
The buildings themselves were also deteriorating and becoming run-down, petty crime was on the rise and the garden was considered unsafe.
建筑物本身也在恶化，破旧不堪，轻微犯罪上升，花园被视为不安全。
In 2002, Housing New Zealand decided the properties needed upgrading.
2002年，新西兰住房部门认定这批住宅需要改造。
The question was, how to avoid repeating the mistakes of the past?
问题是，如何避免重蹈过去的覆辙？
paragraphs.gist: 七十年代末以后居民间出现隔阂，建筑失修、轻微犯罪增加，花园也不再令人安心，促使住房部门在 2002 年决定翻新。

paragraphs.brief: 混合房型与开放视线的设计
sentences: One controversial aspect of the upgrade is that the new development has actually made the density of housing in Talbot Park greater, putting 52 more homes on the same site.
换代的一个有争议的方面是，新的发展实际上使塔尔博特公园的住房密度增大，在同一地点又增加了52个住房。
Doing this required a fresh approach that can be summed up as ‘mix and match’.
这样做需要一种新的方法，可以归纳为“混合和匹配”。

The first priority was to mix up the housing by employing a variety of plans by different architects: some of the accommodation is free-standing houses, some semi-detached, some low-level, multi-apartment blocks.
首要做法是由不同建筑师提供多样方案，将独栋住宅、半独立式住宅和低层多户公寓搭配起来。
By doing this, the development avoids the uniform appearance of so many state-housing projects, which residents complain denies them any sense of individual identity.
通过这样做，发展避免了如此之多的国有住房项目的统一外观，居民抱怨说这剥夺了他们任何个人身份感。
The next goal was to prevent overspending by using efficient designs to maximise the sense of space from minimum room sizes.
下一个目标是，通过使用高效的设计，使最小房间面积的空间感最大化，防止超支。
There was also a no-frills, industrial approach to kitchens, bathrooms and flooring, to optimise durability and ensure the project did not go over budget.
厨房、浴室和地材也采用朴素实用的工业化做法，既提高耐用性，又控制工程预算。
Architecturally, the buildings are relatively conservative: fairly plain houses standing in a small garden.
从建筑造型看，这些房子相当保守：外观简洁，各自坐落在小花园中。
There’s a slight reflection of the traditional Pacific beach house (a fale) but it’s not over-played.
它们略微呼应太平洋地区的传统海滨房屋 fale，但并未刻意夸张这种元素。
‘It seems to us that low-cost housing is about getting as much amenity as you can for the money,’ says architect Michael Thompson.
建筑师迈克尔·汤普森说：「在我们看来，低成本住房就是用有限的钱尽可能提高居住便利度。」
Another key aspect of the ‘mix and match’ approach is openness: one that not only lets residents see what is going on but also lets them know they are seen.
“混合和匹配”方法的另一个关键方面是开放性：它不仅让居民看到正在发生的事情，而且让他们知道他们被看到。

The plan ensures there are no cul-de-sacs or properties hidden from view, that the gardens are not enclosed by trees and that most boundary fences are see-through — a community contained but without walls.
规划确保没有死胡同或隐蔽的住宅，花园不被树木围住，多数边界围栏也能透视，形成一个边界清楚却没有围墙的社区。
paragraphs.gist: 改造在原址增添五十二户，以多种房型避免千篇一律，用紧凑耐用的设计控制预算，并通过通透边界和开放视线兼顾安全。

paragraphs.brief: 灵活住房回应多元文化
sentences: The population today is cosmopolitan: 50% Pacific Islanders, 20% Māori, 15% Asian, 10% New Zealand European and the rest composed of immigrants from Russia, Ukraine and Iran.
今天的人口为世界性：太平洋岛民占50%，毛利人占20%，亚洲人占15%，新西兰欧洲人占10%，其余的人来自俄罗斯、乌克兰和伊朗。
‘It was important that the buildings were sufficiently flexible to cater for the needs of people from a wide variety of cultural backgrounds,’ explains designer James Lundy.
解释设计师詹姆斯・伦迪：“建筑物必须足够灵活，能够满足来自各种文化背景的人的需要。”
paragraphs.gist: 居民来自太平洋岛屿、毛利、亚洲及欧洲等多种文化背景，因此设计者需要让住房布局足够灵活，容纳不同家庭的需要。

paragraphs.brief: 高品质住宅背后的低收入现实
sentences: Despite the quality of the buildings, however, there should be no doubt that Talbot Park and its surrounding suburb of Tāmaki are low socio-economic areas.
然而，尽管建筑物质量很高，但毫无疑问，塔尔博特公园及其周围的塔马基郊区是社会经济低地。
Of the 5,000 houses there, 55% are state houses, 28% privately owned (compared to about 65% nationally) and 17% private rental.
当地五千套住房中，55%为公共住房，28%为私人自有住房（全国约为65%），17%为私人出租住房。
The area has a high density of households with incomes in the $5,000 to $15,000 range and very few with an income over $70,000.
当地许多家庭的收入在五千至一万五千元之间，收入超过七万元的则很少。
That’s in sharp contrast to the more affluent suburbs in Auckland.
这与奥克兰较富裕的郊区形成鲜明对比。
paragraphs.gist: 建筑品质虽高，当地却仍是低收入地区，公房占一半以上，自有住房比例远低于全国水平，高收入家庭也远少于富裕城区。

paragraphs.brief: 密集租务管理与社区交往
sentences: Another important part of the new development is what Housing New Zealand calls ‘intensive tenancy management’.
新发展的另一个重要部分是新西兰住房公司所谓的 " 密集租赁管理 "。
Opponents of the project call it social control.
这个项目的反对者称之为社会控制。
‘The focus is on frequent inspections and setting clear guidelines and boundaries regarding the sort of behaviour we expect from tenants,’ says Graham Bodman, Housing New Zealand’s regional manager.
说，Graham Bodman，住房新西兰的地区经理：“重点是经常检查和就我们期望房客的行为确定明确的指导方针和界限。”
The result is a code of sometimes strict rules: no loud parties after 10 pm; no washing hung over balcony rails; and a requirement to mow lawns and keep the property tidy.
由此形成的规则有时相当严格：晚上十点以后不得举办吵闹聚会，不得在阳台栏杆上晾衣，并须修剪草坪、保持住宅整洁。
The Tenancy Manager walks the site every day, knows everyone by name and deals with problems quickly.
租务经理每天巡视社区，叫得出每个人的名字，出了问题也会迅速处理。
‘It’s all based on the intensification,’ says project manager Stuart Bracey.
项目经理斯图尔特·布雷西说：「这些安排都是因为居住密度提高了。」

‘We acknowledge that if you are going to ask people to live in these quite tightly-packed communities, you have to actually help them to get to know each other by organising morning teas and street barbecues.’
”我们承认，如果你要要求人们生活在这些非常紧凑的社区里，你就必须通过组织晨茶和街头烧烤来帮助他们相互了解。
So far it seems to be working and many involved in the project believe Talbot Park represents the way forward for state housing.
到目前为止，这种做法看来有效，不少参与者相信塔尔博特公园代表了公共住房未来可走的方向。
paragraphs.gist: 密集租务管理既规定噪声和日常维护、由经理每日巡查，也以茶会和街头烧烤帮助相邻住户熟悉彼此，尽管有人视之为社会控制。

lead: Talbot Park, a housing project in Auckland, New Zealand, was once described as a ghetto, troubled by high rates of crime and vandalism.
新西兰奥克兰的塔尔博特公园住宅区曾被称为贫民区，犯罪和蓄意损坏公物的情况十分突出。
However, it has just been rebuilt at a cost of $48 m and the project reflects some new thinking about urban design.
如今，这个社区已斥资约 4,800 万新西兰元完成重建，项目也体现了城市设计方面的一些新思路。
